title: Grant lines in the adopted budget against grants spent and nonprofit payments
question: Where does the published grant line understate what a department actually pays out in grants?
finding: The Human Rights Commission's adopted budget shows a grant line of $1.55 million for fiscal 2024; the ledger records $19.21 million of grants that year, and $71.7 million against $12.0 million budgeted over fiscal 2019 to 2026. Most of the difference was appropriated as an unitemised 'Programmatic Projects' amount ($13.1 million in fiscal 2024, $35.2 million in 2025) or came from grants received. Public Health budgets its nonprofit work as services, not grants, so its ratio says nothing.
how: Character City Grant Program, all funds: adopted budget against the ledger, fiscal 2019 to 2026; beside it, the Controller's nonprofit payment file for the same years. Departments with at least $20 million of grants spent or nonprofit payments.
limits: Departments can budget nonprofit work as grants, as professional services or as a project amount spent later as grants; continuing-project money carries over between years. A large ratio shows a budget line that does not describe the spending, not spending without approval.
